brief: Goldman Sachs' Industrials & Materials desk opens with markets color (ASML's outlook boost lifts tech futures; crude bid up on Middle East attacks; IEA sees diesel constrained into 2027) before three analytical threads. First, China's September CPI (+0.9% yoy) and PPI (+5.0% yoy) beats drive GS to revise 2026/27 PPI forecasts up and CPI forecasts down, while China's trade surplus hit a record $133.5bn on broad-based export and import growth. Second, GS previews US September CPI, expecting core +0.24% (above 0.2% consensus) on an autos pickup and firmer airfares, with benign shelter keeping the print from running hotter, and expects the pace to slow into Q4 on shutdown-related distortions and fading tariff effects. Third, AZZ beat Q2 estimates on EPS, revenue and EBITDA and raised full-year guidance. Separately, GIR upgrades TT to Buy and downgrades LII/CARR to Neutral, arguing Applied HVAC's outperformance continues on stronger estimate revisions and AI/data-center-driven backlog, while Resi HVAC faces tougher competition. A pickup-truck note argues GM's 2026 Sierra/Silverado refresh should lift sales for 2-3 years based on prior Ford/GM/Stellantis refresh cycles, though GM guides volumes flattish through 2027 before the benefit shows more in 2028.
